timeout.recommendation: Add context timeout of 60s for upload, 10s for delete operations

retry.recommendation: Add retry with exponential backoff for transient storage errors

circuit_breaker.recommendation: Add circuit breaker for storage operations to fail fast when storage is down

bulkhead.recommendation: Limit concurrent storage operations to prevent resource exhaustion

fallback.recommendation: Return 503 Service Unavailable when storage is unreachable

idempotency.reason: Upload uses unique UUID, so retry creates a new file. Delete is idempotent (already handles ErrNotExist).

blast_radius.impact: Users cannot upload or delete release attachments when storage is down. Existing attachments remain accessible via DB metadata.

findings.detail: No timeout on storage.Attachments.Save for file upload
DB insert and storage save are in a transaction (db.WithTx), so partial failure rolls back

endpoint_resiliency.cascading_failure_risk: Storage failure prevents all attachment uploads

findings.detail: DB record deleted first, then storage file deleted. If storage delete fails, orphaned file remains but record is gone.
findings.recommendation: Log orphaned files for cleanup; current code already handles ErrNotExist gracefully

non_atomic_operations: DB delete + storage delete are not atomic; storage failure leaves orphaned file
endpoint_resiliency.cascading_failure_risk: Storage failure leaves orphaned files but delete still succeeds from user perspective
endpoint_resiliency.graceful_degradation: Partial - DB record removed even if storage delete fails (logs warning)

rate_limiting.detail: No rate limiting on attachment upload endpoints
rate_limiting.recommendation: Add rate limiting for POST endpoints to prevent abuse

dead_letter_queues.detail: No async flows in these endpoints

single_points_of_failure: Object storage backend - no redundancy or fallback configured
cascading_failure_paths: Storage down → ep-354 upload fails → users cannot attach files to releases
